questions.stem: A man presents with a mixed infection of Plasmodium vivax and Plasmodium falciparum in a health centre in Rajasthan. What is the dosage of the treatment given on the second day?

options.label: A
options.text: 4 tablets of Artesunate 50mg + 6 tablets of Primaquine 2.5mg

options.label: B
options.text: 4 tablets of Artesunate 50mg + 6 tablets of Primaquine 7.5mg

options.label: C
options.text: 4 tablets of Artesunate 50mg 49.05% + Sulphadoxine 1500mg + 6 tablets of Primaquine 2.5mg

options.label: D
options.text: 4 tablets of Artesunate 45mg + Sulphadoxine 1500mg + 6 tablets of Primaquine 7.5mg

questions.answerText: 4 tablets of Artesunate 50mg + 6 tablets of Primaquine 2.5mg
questions.solutionHtml:
4 tablets of Artesunate 50mg + 6 tablets of Primaquine 2.5mg

Mixed P. falciparum and P. vivax infection:

  • This is to be treated as falciparum malaria with ACT other than artesunate + sulfa-pyrimethamine, because sulfa-pyrimethamine is not effective against P. vivax. Anti relapse treatment with a 14-day course of primaquine may be started concurrently.
  • Artesunate plus Sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine is given on 1st day, and from 2nd day artesunate plus primaquine.


Essentials of Medical Pharmacology by KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page No. 877-878

questions.stem: Which of the following beta-adrenergic blockers are beneficial for patients with reduced ejection fraction and can reduce mortality in chronic heart failure without causing exacerbations over a few years?
questions.solutionHtml:
Bisoprolol
  • Beta blocker approved for chronic CHF are metoprolol, bisoprolol and carvedilol. Hence, option D is correct.
  • Introduced gradually and maintained for long term, these drugs retard the progression of CHF and prolong life.
  • The benefit may result from antagonism of deleterious effects of sympathetic overactivity (invoked reflexly by heart failure) on the myocardium.


Essentials of Medical Pharmacology by KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page No. 164-165

questions.stem: A 75-year-old female presented with urinary incontinence. She also has cognitive decline and dementia. Which of the following drugs is useful for treating urinary incontinence?
questions.solutionHtml:
Tolterodine
  • Tolterodine is a M3 selective muscarinic antagonist that has preferential action on urinary bladder; It is indicated in overactive bladder with urinary frequency and urgency.


Essentials of Medical Pharmacology by KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page No. 129

questions.stem: Which drug is used to treat multiple myeloma that is known to cause reactivation of Herpes Zoster?
questions.solutionHtml:
Bortezomib
  • Bortezomib is a first-generation inhibitor of proteasome-mediated protein degradation that has a central role in the treatment of MM.
  • It has immunosuppressant properties and can reactivate herpes zoster virus.
  • Patients should receive antiviral prophylaxis if they are receiving therapy with bortezomib.


Goodman and Gilman's The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 13th Edition, Page No. 1227

questions.stem: A patient presented with breathing difficulty and nasal polyposis when he took aspirin for fever. He faced this issue previously too when he took aspirin. Which among the following is not true about this?

options.label: A
options.text: There is no allergic sensitization to aspirin and its metabolites

options.label: C
options.text: Occur on exposure to only aspirin

options.label: D
options.text: Occurs with exposure to other NSAIDs too that block COX 1

questions.answerText: Occur on exposure to only aspirin
questions.solutionHtml:
Occur on exposure to only aspirin
  • Aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease (AERD), also known as Samter’s Triad, is a chronic medical condition that consists of three clinical features: asthma, sinus disease with recurrent nasal polyps, and sensitivity to aspirin and other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) that inhibit an enzyme called cyclooxygenase-1.
  • The characteristic feature of AERD is that patients develop reactions to aspirin and other NSAIDs. Hence, option C is incorrect.


Essentials of Medical Pharmacology by KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page No. 214-215

questions.stem: A 7-year-old boy presents with a two-week history of persistent fever, fatigue, and pallor. His parents also report easy bruising and gum bleeding. On examination, he is pale with petechiae on his legs, hepatosplenomegaly, and generalized lymphadenopathy. Blood tests show severe anemia, thrombocytopenia, and elevated white blood cell count with blast cells. What is the most appropriate initial treatment regimen for this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Prednisolone + Vincristine
  • This clinical symptom is suggestive of childhood leukemia.
  • Vincristine with glucocorticoids is the treatment of choice to induce remissions in patients with childhood leukemia and in combination with alkylating agents and anthracycline for those with pediatric sarcomas.
  • Vincristine is tolerated better by children than by adults, who may experience severe, progressive neurological toxicity and require lowering of the dose


Goodman and Gilman's The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 13th Edition, Page No. 1187

questions.stem: A hypertensive patient with chronic kidney disease was having frequent attacks of renal colic. Which of the following diuretics is used?
questions.solutionHtml:
Hydrochlorothiazide
  • Hydrochlorothiazide is used in Hypercalciuria with recurrent calcium stones in the kidney. Thiazides act by reducing Ca2+ excretion. Hence, option C is correct.


Essentials of Medical Pharmacology by KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page No. 630-631

questions.stemHtml: Identify the drug marked as 'X' in the image:tPA - Tissue Plasminogen Activator
questions.solutionHtml:
Amino caproic acid

● X drug is Amino caproic acid. ε-Aminocaproic acid and tranexamic acid are lysine analogues that compete for lysine binding sites on plasminogen and plasmin, thereby blocking their interaction with fibrin.

● Therefore, these agents inhibit fibrinolysis and can reverse states that are associated with excessive fibrinolysis.



Goodman and Gilman's The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 13th Edition, Page No. 596

questions.stem: Which drug is used for maintenance therapy in opium addiction?
questions.solutionHtml:
Buprenorphine
  • Buprenorphine, a partial agonist at the MOR, represents a major change in the treatment of opiate addiction.
  • This drug produces minimal withdrawal symptoms when discontinued and has a low potential for overdose, a long duration of action, and the ability to block heroin effects, hence used for maintenance therapy in opium addiction.


Goodman and Gilman's The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 13th Edition, Page No. 439

questions.stem: A patient who recently underwent surgery has complaints of nausea and vomiting. He was prescribed a drug called aprepitant. What is its mechanism of action?
questions.solutionHtml:
NK-1 antagonist
  • Aprepitant is a selective, high affinity NK1 receptor antagonist that blocks the emetic action of substance P, with little effect on 5 HT3 and D2 or other receptors.


Essentials of Medical Pharmacology by KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page No. 718

questions.stem: Arrange the sequence of steps involved at neuromuscular junction end plate potential.

options.label: A
options.text: Acetylcholine release - Calcium entry- Na+ entry

options.label: B
options.text: Calcium entry- Acetylcholine release- Na+ entry

options.label: C
options.text: Na+ entry - Calcium entry - Acetylcholine release

options.label: D
options.text: Na+ entry - Acetylcholine release - Calcium entry

questions.answerText: Calcium entry- Acetylcholine release- Na+ entry
questions.solutionHtml:
Calcium entry- Acetylcholine release- Na+ entry
  • On arrival of action potential , there is opening of voltage gated calcium channels through which calcium influx occurs, leading to calcium mediated exocytosis of acetylcholine and finally Na+ influx results in local depolarization and formation of endplate potential


G K Pal, Comprehensive Textbook of Medical Physiology, 1st Edition, Volume 1, Page No.243

questions.stem: The patient presented with alcoholic gait, and abnormal eye movements (nystagmus) after RTA. Which lobe of the cerebellum is likely affected? RTA - Road Traffic Accident
questions.solutionHtml:
Flocculonodular Lobe
    • The clinical features of patient are due to damage in flocculonodular lobe (vestibulocerebellum, which is concerned with equilibrium and eye movements)
    • Rest of options are incorrect


G K Pal, Comprehensive Textbook of Medical Physiology, 1st Edition, Volume 2, Page No.1089,Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page No. 575

questions.stem: The functioning of the thyroid involves the transport of iodine from the blood to the thyroid follicle. lodine is transported from the follicle to the colloid. Which pump or channel is for transport of iodine from the follicle to the colloid?
questions.solutionHtml:
Pendrin
  • Pendrin ( anion exchanger [ Cl-I- exchanger] ) is an iodine transporter located on apical surface of thyroid cells that transports iodine actively from thyroid cells into colloid
  • Mutations in pendrin gene lead to Pendred syndrome, which is characterised by defective organification of iodine, goitre and sensorineural deafness


Reference: Guyton and Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th Edition, Page No.: 942, G K Pal, Comprehensive Textbook of Medical Physiology, 1st Edition, Volume 1, Page No.: 485

questions.stem: The resting membrane potential (RMP) of the nerve is -70mV. Increased permeability of which ion is responsible for the RMP?
questions.solutionHtml:
Potassium
  • Resting membrane potential is generated by the K+ that leaks from the inside of the cell to the outside via leak K+ channels and generates a negative charge in the inside of the membrane vs the outside.
  • At rest, the membrane is impermeable to Na+, as all of the Na+ channels are closed.


Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page No. 221, Guyton And Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th Edition, Page No. 68

questions.stem: Renal compensation in metabolic acidosis takes time because:

options.label: A
options.text: Initially the pH of tubular fluid increases

options.label: B
options.text: Low pH normally decreases bicarbonate excretion

options.label: C
options.text: It takes hours to days for kidney to synthesize enzymes that produce NH4+

options.label: D
options.text: Other ions in the tubule interfere with buffer action

questions.answerText: It takes hours to days for kidney to synthesize enzymes that produce NH4+
questions.solutionHtml:
It takes hours to days for kidney to synthesize enzymes that produce NH4+
  • Metabolic acidosis is the condition of primary bicarbonate deficit that results from excessive removal of bicarbonate into urine in order to buffer the extra acids of the body.
  • To restore acid-base balance, the kidneys initiate a complex set of responses that include increased ammonia genesis and gluconeogenesis, enhanced acid and ammonium ion excretion, and a net production and release of bicarbonate ions.


G K Pal, Comprehensive Textbook of Medical Physiology, 1st Edition, Volume 1, Page No.: 1269,1270,Guyton and Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th Edition, Page No.: 418
